uncited: This family addresses the limitations of standard 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) regarding memory efficiency, rendering quality at varying scales, and structural coherence in large or complex scenes.

While standard 3DGS uses a flat list of Gaussians, these methods introduce hierarchy, graph connectivity, or dynamic adaptation to optimize training, reduce memory footprint, and eliminate artifacts like aliasing or boundary discontinuities.

They differ from siblings like [TurboGS](15697-turbogs.md) (which focuses on rasterization speed) and [Data Compression](12943-data-compression-and-storage-optimization.md) (which focuses on storage) by modifying the geometric representation or optimization graph itself.
All methods in this family modify the standard 3DGS primitive set or its optimization/rendering pipeline to introduce structure or adaptivity.

*   **Primitive Representation:** Gaussians are defined by mean $\mathbf{\mu}$, covariance $\mathbf{\Sigma}$ (derived from scale $\mathbf{s}$ and rotation $\mathbf{q}$), opacity $\alpha$, and spherical harmonics coefficients $\mathbf{c}$ .
where $N_{active}$ are the Gaussians overlapping the pixel .
*   **Adaptivity:** Methods either partition the scene (graph/tree), select a subset of primitives (dynamic), or deform primitives based on view scale (adaptive) .
However, standard 3DGS suffers from high memory usage, boundary artifacts in large scenes, and aliasing at varying zoom levels.
Recent research has focused on hierarchical structures (octrees, graphs) and adaptive mechanisms to improve scalability and quality.
Hierarchical Anchor Coupling  addresses feature propagation in hierarchical representations.
